# libngspice-hefesto

Hefesto's simulation engine: ngspice-47 with a small Hefesto patch series, built
by a Hefesto-written CMake wrapper as one replaceable shared library,
`libngspice-hefesto` (Q-SIM-7, Q-SIM-20, Q-SIM-26; approved 2026-11-22).
Plan: `openspec/changes/m9-lvs-simulation` design D2 and D9, task 5.1.
Capability `simulation-engine-embedding`, requirements "ngspice embedded as a
library" and "ngspice build configuration and license hygiene".

Only the worker `hefesto-simd` loads the library, through the
`hefesto-ngspice-adapter` plugin (task 5.4). The editor, `hefesto-cli` and the
core never link it.

## What is here

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `pin.json` | The pin: ngspice-47, tag commit `a80f6e3e95d5…`, the release tarball's URLs and SHA-256, the patch level, the configure feature line, the code-model libraries. Single source of truth. |
| `patches/series`, `patches/000N-*.patch` | The patch series, applied in order with `patch -p1`; each patch's justification is the comment above it in `series`. |
| `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/` | The wrapper: fetch, patch, `config.h`, the code models, the registries, the library, the optional executable, the manifest and the source archive. |
| `cmake/sources.cmake` | GENERATED by `tools/gen_sources.py`: the files ngspice's own build compiles for the feature line, with their include paths and defines. |
| `src/` | Hefesto glue called by patches 0001 and 0002 (built-in OSDI and code-model registries). Apache-2.0. |
| `tools/ngspice_manifest.py` | Writes `ngspice-manifest.json`, refuses a build that compiles a GPL file, writes the source archive, checks a manifest. |
| `tools/sync_image_copy.py` | Copies the build inputs to `tools/golden/container/ngspice/`, the golden capture image's build context (Q-SIM-23 (a)). |
| `tests/` | Unit tests of the manifest tool, and regression tests of each patch on a built library (`ngspice_harness.py` drives the C API with ctypes). |

## Building

From Hefesto's top level (off by default, so normal builds are unaffected):

    cmake --preset macos-debug -DHEFESTO_BUILD_NGSPICE=ON
    cmake --build --preset macos-debug --target ngspice-hefesto

On its own (this is what `.github/workflows/ngspice.yml` and the capture image do):

    cmake -S third_party/ngspice -B build/ngspice -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          [-DHEFESTO_NGSPICE_EXECUTABLE=ON]
    cmake --build build/ngspice -j4
    cmake --build build/ngspice --target ngspice_hefesto_source_archive

Outputs in the build directory: `libngspice-hefesto.{so,dylib}`, `ngspice`
(with `HEFESTO_NGSPICE_EXECUTABLE=ON`), `ngspice-manifest.json`,
`ngspice-hefesto-<version>-src.tar.gz`. Requirements: a C11 and C++11 compiler,
CMake 3.25, Python 3, `patch`, network access for the first configure (or a
populated `FETCHCONTENT_BASE_DIR`).

Tests:

    python3 -m unittest discover -s third_party/ngspice/tests        # manifest tests only
    HEFESTO_NGSPICE_LIB=$PWD/build/ngspice/libngspice-hefesto.dylib \
    HEFESTO_NGSPICE_EXE=$PWD/build/ngspice/ngspice \
        python3 -m unittest discover -s third_party/ngspice/tests -v    # plus the patch tests

## Build configuration

- Feature line (simulation-engine-embedding feature table): KLU on (bundled),
  OSDI on, XSPICE on with the `analog`, `digital` (without `d_cosim`),
  `spice2poly` and `xtradev` code models compiled in and registered statically;
  `table`, `xtraevt`, `tlines`, FFTW3, CIDER/NDEV, `d_cosim` and its Icarus/GHDL
  shims, readline/editline, X11 and OpenMP off.
- `-ffp-contract=off` on every ngspice object (Q-SIM-10); no `-ffast-math`.
- `-fvisibility=hidden`: the library exports only the ngspice C API
  (`ngSpice_*`, `ngGet_*`, `ngCM_Input_Path`).
- ngspice's own sources are compiled with `-w`: they do not build cleanly
  under Hefesto's warning set, and their warnings are not Hefesto's to fix. The
  glue in `src/` is compiled with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`.
- `config.h` is written by the wrapper (`cmake/config.h.in`), with the host
  probes of `cmake/NgspiceProbes.cmake`. The version string is
  `<release>-hefesto<level>` (now `47-hefesto1`), the build date is empty.

## The patch series

| Patch | Why | Changes results? |
|---|---|---|
| 0001 static OSDI registry | `osdi`/`pre_osdi` resolve built-in modules by basename; other files load only while `hefesto_osdi_static_only` is unset | no |
| 0002 static code-model registration | code models compiled in, registered when the device table is created; `codemodel` of a built-in library opens no file | no |
| 0003 portable seeding | the Tausworthe states come from SplitMix64 of the seed, not from the C library's `rand()` | yes, every random draw (on purpose) |
| 0004 deterministic initialisation | Gaussian pool seeded from the last seed, not the pid; `setseed` refills it; `ngSpice_nospiceinit()` honoured on hosts with `pwd.h`; no crash when `ngSpice_nospinit()`/`ngSpice_nospiceinit()` run before `ngSpice_Init()` | yes, trnoise/trrandom draws (on purpose) |

Raise `hefesto_level` in `pin.json` whenever the series changes. A cached,
patched tree records the series it carries (`.hefesto-patch-series`) and keeps
a copy of the applied patches (`.hefesto-applied/`). Editing a patch or the
series re-runs the configure, which reverses the old series (last patch first)
and applies the new one; only a tree patched before those copies existed asks
for its directory to be deleted.

## Rebuilding or replacing the library (LGPL)

The library is meant to be replaceable by the user (design D2, "Replaceability"):

1. Unpack the source archive that ships with the release
   (`ngspice-hefesto-<version>-src.tar.gz`; it holds every compiled ngspice file
   as patched, the whole `src/osdi` tree as MPL-2.0 section 3.2 requires, the
   code-model inputs, the patches and this wrapper), or use the pinned tarball
   and `patches/`.
2. Change what you want, then build as above (`ngspice-manifest.json` records
   the configure feature line and the patches).
3. Put the new library into the install's `lib/` directory, replacing the
   versioned file (`libngspice-hefesto.47.<level>.dylib`,
   `libngspice-hefesto.so.47.<level>`) and keeping its links; `hefesto-simd`
   in `bin/` finds it through the install-relative run path
   (`$ORIGIN/../lib` / `@loader_path/../lib`). Keep the exported C API unchanged.
4. macOS: sign the versioned file ad hoc
   (`codesign --force -s - lib/libngspice-hefesto.47.<level>.dylib`);
   `hefesto-simd` alone carries `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation`
   so it can load it. `docs/building.md` gives the full steps (INTEGRATION task).

The desktop linking (a replaceable shared library loaded only by the separate
worker process) goes through a legal review before the Desktop Beta (D-28,
design D2, task 20.1); that review may change the link type.

## Updating the pin

1. Change `pin.json` (release, tag commit, archive URLs and SHA-256) and run
   `python3 third_party/ngspice/tools/gen_sources.py --src <unpacked tree> --work <scratch>`.
2. Refresh the patches until `cmake` applies them, and raise `hefesto_level`.
3. Run `python3 third_party/ngspice/tools/sync_image_copy.py` and update
   `[tools.ngspice]` in `tools/golden/pins.toml` (tools/golden/tests/test_pins.py
   checks both).

## Licences

`ngspice-manifest.json` lists every component with the licence ngspice's
`COPYING` gives it and the notices its files carry: ngspice (Modified BSD),
KLU, AMD, COLAMD, BTF and SuiteSparse_config (`src/maths/KLU`, LGPLv2 per
`COPYING`; COLAMD's files say LGPL 2.1 or later, `UFconfig.h` says "no
licensing restrictions"), numparam (LGPLv2 or newer), OSDI and cppduals
(MPL-2.0), sparse (MIT style) and the XSPICE code models (public domain). The
manifest step fails if a compiled file carries a GPL notice (Bison's output,
with its special exception, is allowed). OpenVAF (GPL-3.0) is used only as a
build-time tool in the capture image (and, from task 5.2, to compile the IHP
OSDI modules); it is never linked or shipped.
